lead: >-
  Over 8 days, this route takes you through Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Perito Moreno Glacier, Puerto Natales, Torres del Paine and Santiago. The tour includes accommodation, guides, transfers and excursions. Domestic flights starting at $850 per person and international flights are paid separately.

## Patagonia in 8 Days: Two National Parks on Opposite Sides of the Border

The journey's main natural highlights are [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Argentina and Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). A road transfer and border crossing connect them, while the city visits are divided between [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

The program lasts **8 days and 7 nights**. This private itinerary offers a chance to see different parts of Patagonia during a short vacation. It is also busy: transfers and flights alternate with excursions, leaving little time for extended independent hikes.

## Perito Moreno and El Calafate

From Buenos Aires, the journey continues to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). Here, the program includes the Nativo Experience excursion along Lake Argentino, while the following day is dedicated to [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/) and Perito Moreno Glacier.

The principal way to see the glacier is from a network of viewing walkways that reveal its face from different distances and elevations. The distinctive blue crevasses and falling blocks of ice make every visit slightly different. Major ice-calving events cannot be guaranteed at any particular time.

Viewing the glacier from the platforms is not the same as walking on its surface: ice trekking requires special equipment and separate guidance. The main tour does not list it as an included activity. A warm windproof jacket, rain protection and comfortable footwear are useful at the viewpoints.

## Crossing the Border Through the Patagonian Steppe

After the Argentine glacier, the route heads across the Chilean border to [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). This is a full day on the road through Patagonian landscapes. Border-control times vary, so tight connections and plans for additional evening excursions require caution.

Travelers need the appropriate documents for their individual nationality. Chile applies sanitary and customs restrictions, including rules on bringing in food and materials of plant or animal origin. It is sensible to check the contents of your luggage in advance.

## Torres del Paine and Santiago

A separate day is devoted to Chile's Torres del Paine National Park. Instead of a single glacier face, visitors encounter broad valleys, granite peaks, lakes and stretches of southern steppe. Trail access depends on the season, precipitation, wind and decisions made by the park authorities.

The day excursion offers a chance to see Patagonia's celebrated scenery, but **it is not the multi-day W Trek**. [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/) is also in the region; the actual stops should be checked against the day's itinerary.

The final flight takes travelers to Santiago de Chile for a sightseeing tour, bringing the journey to a close with an introduction to the second country's capital.

## Tour Price and Additional Expenses

Our tour starts **at $3939**. The price includes accommodation in the listed or comparable hotels, guides, transfers, excursions, entrance tickets and meals as specified in the program. Items charged separately include **domestic flights from $850 per person**, international flights, additional excursions, food and drinks beyond those specified, tips and personal expenses.

To compare trip costs, add both types of flights and your individual expenses to the base price. If you would like to combine Patagonia with Easter Island and Chile's wine valleys, consider the [12-day itinerary through both countries](/multi-country/tour/active-adventure-tour/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Eight Days in Patagonia

### Does the tour visit both countries?

Yes. The program begins in Argentina, then crosses into Chile and finishes in Santiago.

### Is a walk on Perito Moreno's ice included?

The program includes a visit to the glacier, but a separate ice climb or glacier trek is not listed among the included services.

### Are flights included?

No. Domestic flights starting at $850 per person and international tickets are paid for separately.

## Chilean Fjords and Patagonia in 9 Days: An Expedition Cruise

The [Patagonia and Chilean Fjords cruise](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) connects the Chilean and Argentine regions of the continent's far south. On one of the described sailing directions, the vessel departs from [Puerto Montt](/chile/place/valdivia-puerto-montt/), travels through Chile's fjords and channels, the areas of San Rafael and Bernardo O'Higgins national parks, the Strait of Magellan and Tierra del Fuego, and ends the voyage in [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/).

The journey lasts **9 days and 8 nights**. This is an expedition cruise: guests spend most of their time aboard the ship, while boat outings and possible landings depend on wind, waves, ice conditions and the crew's navigational decisions. The voyage may also operate in the reverse direction. Exact ports, their order and embarkation times must be matched to the particular departure.

## Main Stages of the Voyage

| Day | Area of the Route |
|---|---|
| 1 | Puerto Montt |
| 2 | Puyuhuapi Channel |
| 3 | San Rafael |
| 4 | Gulf of Penas |
| 5 | Caleta Tortel |
| 6 | Bernardo O'Higgins |
| 7 | Strait of Magellan |
| 8 | Beagle Channel |
| 9 | Ushuaia |

After boarding in Puerto Montt, the expedition heads south through the Gulf of Corcovado. In the Aysén region, the route crosses a network of islands and narrow passages. Sightings of dolphins, sea lions and birds depend on natural conditions; wildlife cannot be guaranteed at a specific place or hour.

Near [San Rafael National Park](/chile/place/laguna-san-rafael-national-park/), the journey passes the glacial landscapes of the Northern Patagonian Ice Field. Sections of open water, [Caleta Tortel](/chile/place/caleta-tortel/) and Messier Channel follow. Day six is associated with [Bernardo O'Higgins National Park](/chile/place/bernardo-ohiggins-national-park/), large parts of which encompass the fjords and glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Access to these areas is mainly by water.

The final stages pass through the Strait of Magellan, Tierra del Fuego, the Beagle Channel and [Garibaldi Fjord](/chile/place/garibaldi-fjord/). Disembarkation is planned for day nine in Ushuaia, an Argentine city near the southern tip of the island of Tierra del Fuego.

## Expedition Landings: Why the Itinerary May Change

Narrow channels, glaciers and exposed stretches of the Southern Ocean create particular challenges. Opportunities to take small boats ashore, disembark or alter the sequence of stops are determined by the weather and safe navigation. Even when a day-by-day itinerary has been published, access to every viewpoint and a landing at each named location cannot be guaranteed.

Sailing from one region to another is an important part of the experience in itself: deep fjords, rocky shores and glacial valleys unfold from the deck. This is what distinguishes an expedition cruise from a land-based [Patagonia trip](/interests/wildlife/), where travelers spend most of their time on trails and road routes.

## What Is Included on Board

The program includes the cruise, guided excursions, onboard lectures, information materials, the use of waterproof boots and port fees. Meals comprise buffet breakfasts and lunches, and dinners with a choice of main courses. Drinks from the specified categories are included with lunch and dinner; tea, coffee, water and snacks are available during the day.

Additional flights, transfers and accommodation outside the cruise, travel insurance, gratuities, personal purchases, communication and laundry services, and bar purchases are charged separately. Visa and passport requirements depend on nationality and the actual border crossings, so they should be checked for the particular itinerary and ports rather than for the expedition's general title.

## Choosing a Departure and Preparing for the Voyage

When comparing sailings, confirm the embarkation and disembarkation ports, the ship's direction of travel, transfers included before boarding and after arrival, the actual cabin category, group size and restrictions on boat landings. Layered clothing works best: a waterproof jacket, warm layers, gloves and shoes suitable for a wet deck are useful even in relatively mild weather.

If city walks, road journeys or more time in national parks on land are important to you, compare [other cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) with conventional [tours of Chile](/chile/tour/). A fjord expedition primarily offers the opportunity to explore a hard-to-reach coast from the sea.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Cruise

### Does the route always start in Puerto Montt?

No. Depending on the departure, it runs from north to south or in the opposite direction. The exact port is specified in the conditions for each sailing.

### Are all landings guaranteed?

No. Sea and ice conditions may change the order of excursions and whether the shore can be reached. The crew makes the safety decisions.

### Are flights and insurance included?

Additional flights, travel insurance and services outside the cruise are listed as exclusions. The full cost should be checked against the particular departure date.

## Patagonia and the Uyuni Salt Flat in 12 Days: Argentina, Chile and Bolivia

**This 12-day itinerary combines 3 countries and 2 dramatically different landscapes: glacial Patagonia and the high-altitude salt flats of Bolivia.** The journey begins in Buenos Aires, travels through Argentina's [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Chilean Patagonia and Santiago, and ends with the Altiplano's lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

The program suits travelers who want to see **Perito Moreno Glacier, Torres del Paine National Park and the Uyuni salt plain** in a single trip while also spending time in major cities. It is a busy journey: transfers and changes of climate take up a significant share of the time.

## How the 12 Days Are Divided

| Period | Main Stage |
|---|---|
| Days 1–4 | Buenos Aires, El Calafate and the glacier |
| Days 5–8 | Chilean Patagonia and Santiago |
| Days 9–12 | Altiplano, Uyuni and the return journey |

**Argentina, days 1–4.** On arrival, you will be met and transferred to your accommodation. The following day features a private tour of Buenos Aires, including historic neighborhoods, major city squares and tango. You then travel to El Calafate. From here, a group excursion visits [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), where you can watch its ice face from viewing walkways. Los Glaciares National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

**Chile, days 5–8.** The route crosses the border and reaches Puerto Natales. The next day brings a group excursion to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), taking in Mylodon Cave, viewpoints by the lakes and Salto Grande waterfall. Later, the itinerary includes a transfer via Punta Arenas and a flight to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) for a city tour.

**Bolivia, days 9–10.** From Santiago, the route goes via Calama Airport to the Chile–Bolivia border. The off-road section of the Altiplano then begins: Green Lagoon, geothermal areas, Laguna Colorada and other high-altitude lakes, followed by the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and cactus-covered Incahuasi Island. The final 2 days are devoted to returning via Calama to Santiago and concluding the trip.

## Perito Moreno Glacier: What Is Included and What Costs Extra

The excursion to Perito Moreno takes place on day four. Its main purpose is to see the glacier's moving and calving ice face from shore-based viewing platforms. Even without stepping onto the ice, you can appreciate the glacier's width and its position beside Lake Argentino.

**Trekking on the ice itself is a separate optional activity.** Glacier trekking costs **600 USD per person** and is not included in the base price. It requires additional time and compliance with the operator's conditions; visiting the park does not automatically include walking on the glacier.

## Torres del Paine: Sightseeing Excursion or Hiking Trip?

Day six includes an excursion through the national park, with Patagonian steppes, mountain ranges, turquoise lakes and waterfalls. Mylodon Cave is included, and one of the short walking stretches leads to Salto Grande.

This is **a sightseeing day in the park**, not a confirmed multi-day W Trek or a full hike to the base of the granite towers. Longer hikes have their own requirements concerning fitness and trail access. Their availability should be considered separately from the main program.

Chile's CONAF determines official restrictions and access to the trails. Strong winds and sudden weather changes are possible in Patagonia even in summer; warm layers, wind protection and comfortable shoes are useful for the walks.

## High-Altitude Bolivia: Lagoons and Salt Flat

The high-altitude section begins after the flight to Calama and the overland border crossing. Volcanoes, desert plateaus, hot springs and lagoons soon appear. **Red Laguna Colorada** is known for its water color and birds, while nearby lakes may display entirely different shades.

In the dry season, the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) looks like a white plain patterned with geometric salt formations. After rain, a shallow layer of water may form across part of its surface and reflect the sky; route accessibility changes accordingly. The mirror-like panorama cannot be guaranteed for a given date. Water and ground conditions may restrict access to some sections.

Another defining feature is **the altitude of the Altiplano**. Compared with the cities and coastal parts of Patagonia, there is less oxygen here, with sharp differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures. The physical demands should not be judged by distance in kilometers alone.

## Services and Expenses to Compare Before Booking

This tour lasts **12 days and 11 nights**. The 2027 rates vary for single, double and triple occupancy; there is no single price for every group. For example, **with 2 participants sharing a DBL room, the price is 7,198 USD per person**. Flights are charged separately.

Optional services are distinct from the main program: in addition to glacier trekking, there is **a wine excursion to the Maipo Valley** at **276 USD per person**, with a minimum of 2 participants. These amounts should not automatically be added to the base budget. Also consider international and domestic flights, the selected room category and group size.

## Comparison with a Longer Journey

If you would like to add **several days cruising the fjords of Tierra del Fuego and a visit to Argentina's Bariloche**, see the [18-day tour of Argentina, Chile and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/). Its structure is different, with an extended sea passage and more days in the southern part of the continent.

The 12-day itinerary focuses on cities, two Patagonian parks and Bolivia. It suits travelers seeking varied geography in limited time rather than an extended marine expedition.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Patagonia–Uyuni Tour

### Are 12 days enough for 3 countries?

The itinerary relies on flights and road transfers. It allows you to see the main listed attractions but leaves few free days for additional trips.

### Is a full trek in Torres del Paine included?

No. The main day is a group sightseeing excursion around the park. An extended mountain trek is not part of the required itinerary.

### Can you walk on Perito Moreno Glacier?

Ice trekking is available separately for 600 USD per person. The base excursion lets visitors see the glacier from viewing platforms.

### When does Uyuni look like a mirror?

The reflective surface appears when water remains after rainfall. Weather cannot guarantee the effect, and flooding can limit vehicle access to certain sections of the salt flat.

## An 18-Day VIP Tour of Peru and Bolivia: Amazon, Machu Picchu and Uyuni

This itinerary combines the Peruvian Amazon, ancient Andean cities, Lake Titicaca and Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat. Over **18 days and 17 nights**, travelers experience several very different modes of transport and accommodation: the Aria Amazon cruise ship, the Hiram Bingham train, private flights, a helicopter excursion and the domed Kachi Lodge on the salt flat.

The program's value lies in its specific experiences. It appeals to those who want to visit several of South America's best-known destinations while enjoying private excursions and high-end hotels. Even this level of service, however, cannot eliminate changes in altitude and climate or the complex logistics of traveling between remote areas.

## Geography of the Journey, Stage by Stage

| Days | Main Stage |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Lima and museums |
| 3–5 | Amazon, Aria Amazon |
| 6–11 | Cusco, the valley and Machu Picchu |
| 12–13 | Titicaca, Titilaka |
| 14–16 | Bolivia, Uyuni Salt Flat |
| 17–18 | Nazca, Ballestas and departure |

The trip begins in the lower-lying, wetter regions of Peru. The route then moves to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) before reaching Titicaca and the Bolivian Altiplano. The differences between these regions matter when choosing clothing and assessing physical demands.

## Lima and Four Days on the Amazon

The opening days are spent in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/): modern Miraflores, historic neighborhoods, the Santo Domingo monastery and the Larco Museum. The program names Belmond Miraflores Park, as well as culinary stops at Rafael and Central. **Restaurant dinners are paid for separately**, so the appearance of famous restaurants in the itinerary does not mean their meals are included in the package.

On day three, a flight takes travelers to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/), where the **4-day, 3-night Aria Amazon cruise** begins. The ship has 16 suites with panoramic windows, and guests enjoy full board, relaxation areas and premium beverages.

The river portion includes jungle walks, wildlife watching, kayaking and fishing. The actual sequence of landings and river outings is determined by local conditions and the ship's program. Lightweight long-sleeved clothing, insect protection and waterproof storage for personal belongings are useful for the tropical section.

## Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu and the Hiram Bingham Train

After the cruise, the journey continues in the [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) area. Accommodation in the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) is planned at Explora Sacred Valley, with several days of excursions to choose from. The program introduces travelers to Andean communities, local crafts and the valley's natural attractions.

Participants travel to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) on the **Hiram Bingham train**. This part of the journey is an experience in its own right: onboard service and meals are followed by a private bus and a tour of the archaeological complex, then a return journey by train. Accommodation at Belmond Palacio Nazarenas in Cusco is planned after the excursion.

Machu Picchu is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Planning a visit requires attention to the particular entrance ticket and authorized visitor circuit: premium guiding does not replace the site's current rules.

Another special day features **a helicopter flight over Vinicunca**. The flight lasts about 1 hour and 20 minutes, including approximately 10 minutes above Rainbow Mountain itself. This option lets travelers see the colorful slopes without a long hike to an elevation of about 5,200 m, although the flight is still subject to aviation and weather conditions.

## Lake Titicaca and Nights at the Uyuni Salt Flat

On the shore of [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the program provides accommodation at Titilaka and excursions to the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The focus here is on local life, traditional weaving and how the reed islands are constructed.

The journey continues from Peru into Bolivia via La Paz. At the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), guests stay at **Kachi Lodge**, in domed accommodations beside the salt plain. The program mentions Colchani, salt formations, areas where water emerges on the surface and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/). A separate day featuring lagoons, flamingos, Ollagüe Volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat is marked **as optional**.

Seasonality is crucial at Uyuni: a dry salt crust looks very different from a surface covered by reflective water. The famous mirror effect depends on the actual weather on the day and cannot be promised year-round.

## Nazca and Ballestas: The Final Aviation Day

On day seventeen, you will take a private aircraft to the [Nazca Lines](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) and then head to the coast and the Ballestas Islands aboard a private yacht. The Nazca geoglyphs are a UNESCO-listed complex of remarkable pre-Hispanic images on an arid plain.

Around the Ballestas Islands, travelers may see seabirds and animals, including sea lions. Actual weather and safe operating conditions matter for both flights and boat excursions. The final day ends with a transfer to Lima Airport.

## Included Services, Expenses and Preparation

The tour includes **accommodation, excursions, guide services, specified meals and transfers**. International flights and additional activities are outside the package. Certain items, including dinners at Lima restaurants and the optional day on the Altiplano, must not automatically be counted as included.

**The current tour listing has no single confirmed numerical starting price.** When comparing options, consider the chosen hotels and flights, the precise components of the private itinerary and additional activities. With a cruise, a luxury train, private aviation and numerous nights in remote places, the detailed inclusions matter more than the VIP label alone.

The elevations vary considerably: Cusco is about 3,400 m above sea level and Uyuni about 3,600 m. Even though a helicopter replaces the climb on foot at Vinicunca, travelers still spend time in high-altitude cities and on the salt flat. Anyone sensitive to altitude should discuss preparations before traveling.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Peru and Bolivia VIP Itinerary

### How long is the Amazon cruise?

The program provides for **4 days and 3 nights** aboard Aria Amazon, starting in Iquitos.

### How is the visit to Machu Picchu organized?

The program includes the Hiram Bingham train, a private bus and a guided tour of the archaeological complex. The exact entrance time depends on confirmed tickets.

### Is it necessary to hike to Vinicunca?

No. The current program includes **a helicopter flight over the mountain**.

### Is the excursion to Bolivia's colored lagoons compulsory?

No. The additional day on the Altiplano with its lagoons is designated optional. The main itinerary already includes Uyuni Salt Flat and its nearby attractions.

targetPath: /multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/
kind: tour
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Discover the 12-Day Peru and Bolivia Tour"
lead: "This 12-day group itinerary connects Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Titicaca, La Paz and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Uyuni occupies one main excursion day, without a long drive to the southern Altiplano lagoons. We explain the 3★ and 4★ packages, altitude, optional outings and actual expenses."

## Peru and Bolivia in 12 Days: Who Will Enjoy the Uyuni Itinerary?

This program is designed for travelers who want to explore Inca culture and see the Uyuni Salt Flat on one journey without undertaking a lengthy driving expedition across southern Bolivia. The duration is **12 days and 11 nights**, and the format is **a shared group tour from 2 participants**, with specified departure dates in 2027.

The route begins and ends in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). In between are [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), high-altitude Lake Titicaca, [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The defining feature is that several days are devoted to Peru's cultural and historic sites, while the Bolivian salt flat is visited on a full, separate excursion before returning to La Paz.

## How the 12 Days Are Divided

| Days | Main Section |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| 5–7 | Cusco, the road to Titicaca, Bolivia |
| 8–9 | Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz |
| 10–12 | Return to Lima and departure |

A key experience in Peru is the visit to Machu Picchu. The program provides **Expedition-class** train tickets for the Cusco – Aguas Calientes – Cusco route. There is no basis for promising the Hiram Bingham train on this tour: that service features in other, longer premium itineraries. The specific entrance ticket for the archaeological complex also needs to be confirmed.

In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), travelers explore several Inca and colonial-era landmarks. Day five is free: guests may choose a separate excursion to the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) or a trip to Vinicunca, subject to fitness, scheduling and the conditions of the additional activity.

On day six, the road crosses the Andes toward [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Travelers then visit Bolivia's [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) and continue to La Paz. This is a full international border crossing, so entry documents and requirements should be checked for each traveler's citizenship and travel date.

## One Day at Uyuni: What Travelers Will See

Day eight is dedicated to the Uyuni Salt Flat. During the excursion, you will see the expansive salt plain, stops associated with local salt production and sunset tea. The route also includes Colchani and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/); access to particular sections depends on surface and water conditions.

The [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) changes with the seasons. During dry periods, its surface resembles a level white field; in the wet season, rainwater can form a thin reflective layer. NASA describes both conditions and notes that heavy flooding may temporarily restrict some routes. Thus, **a mirror reflection is not guaranteed for any particular date**, and the route across the salt flat may change.

On day nine, travelers return to La Paz and visit the Valley of the Moon. This concludes the main Bolivian nature section. If Laguna Colorada, the Sol de Mañana geysers, the Siloli Desert and hot springs are priorities, compare this tour with the [15-day Altiplano lakes itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/): those attractions have their own dedicated days in the longer program.

## Altitude and Travel Pace

This itinerary is considerably more demanding than staying in a single city. Moving from low-lying Lima to Cusco, and later to Titicaca and La Paz, involves a rapid gain in elevation. According to the CDC, Cusco lies at about **3,350 m** and La Paz at about **3,650 m**; unfamiliar altitude requires acclimatization even without challenging hikes.

Travelers with conditions that could worsen at altitude should discuss the journey with a doctor in advance. During the first days at elevation, it is better to reduce physical exertion and account for temperature swings and strong sunlight. **The optional trip to Vinicunca**, which reaches elevations of around 5,200 m, demands substantially greater stamina and should not be mistaken for an easy compulsory stroll.

One advantage of this particular 12-day program is that it does not include several consecutive days of driving across southern Bolivia's deserts and lagoons. The trade-off for a shorter trip is less time in the natural landscapes of the Altiplano.

## Price, Accommodation Packages and Included Services

The 2027 departures have the following rates **in US dollars per person**, for groups of at least 2 travelers:

| Occupancy | 3★ | 4★ |
|---|---:|---:|
| DBL / TPL | $5346 | $5611 |
| SGL | $6165 | $6632 |

DBL means double occupancy, TPL triple and SGL single occupancy. The day-by-day program describes hotels in the 4★ package; the 3★ package has its own alternatives in the tour's full rate table. Hotels may be replaced by comparable properties in the same category.

The price includes **transfers, specified meals and excursions, entrance tickets listed in the program, the Expedition train**, and flights **Lima – Cusco and La Paz – Uyuni – La Paz**. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the excursions **except for the Titicaca crossing and Uyuni**: the working language on those sections is confirmed separately.

**The La Paz – Lima flight appears in the itinerary but is absent from the list of included air tickets.** Whether it is included, and its price, must be confirmed before payment. Airport taxes, additional excursions, excess baggage and drinks are also listed separately.

For the New Year departure, there is **a $250 net supplement per person**, including a festive dinner and service. Optional experiences include the Sacred Valley, Vinicunca, the Larco Museum and Nazca and Ballestas options; their rates and conditions are available in the tour program. These are independent options and do not become compulsory merely because they are listed in the catalog.

## Choosing Between 12 and 15 Days

The [12-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) is better suited to travelers who prioritize Machu Picchu, Andean cities, Titicaca and **one day on Uyuni's white salt plain**. The [15-day journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) adds the rocky deserts, high-altitude lakes and geothermal fields of southern Bolivia. Its nature section is longer and involves more time on the road.

The choice depends on the time available and willingness to undertake high-altitude road transfers. If the group includes people with different fitness levels, it is best to discuss the planned altitude stops before choosing travel dates.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the 12-Day Tour

### Is Machu Picchu included?

**Yes.** The excursion is part of the main itinerary, and Expedition train tickets are included in the price.

### Does the trip include the lagoons of the southern Altiplano?

**There is no separate multi-day itinerary through the southern lagoons.** The Bolivian nature section focuses on Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz. Lagoons and geysers feature in the 15-day program.

### Is it possible to see the mirror surface at Uyuni?

**Yes, when rainfall and salt-flat conditions are suitable.** The result depends on the actual weather, not on the month name or a promise in a catalog.

### How much does double occupancy cost?

**From $5346 per person in the 3★ package.** The 4★ DBL rate is $5611; additional expenses and the La Paz – Lima flight must be considered separately.

### Are there any free days?

**Yes.** The itinerary includes free days in Cusco and Lima; some excursions can be added for an extra charge.
